components.gap: (a) Fisher pp. 357-358: the sampling law of chi^2 (equivalently 2L) after fitting, the Type III curve with n'-1 degrees of freedom that calibrates goodness of fit, is neither proved nor corrected (body 1678-1682 says that law is not asserted); owed: that law with its exact premises (joint limit of standardized cell counts with the fitting projection) or a stated correction. (b) Fisher p. 337: the claim that from p=1 downwards the weight of the location/end-point determination grows faster than n is left unsettled at p=1 (body 1540-1543); owed: an exact rate statement at p=1 (a statistic achieving a faster-than-root-n rate, or proof that none does). (c) Fisher pp. 346-347, figs. 3-4: the efficiency contours on the Type I/II side of N (y>0) are not shown to be efficiencies of those curves (body 1129-1132); owed with their regularity scope. (d) Fisher p. 348: zero efficiency of the mean when an end exponent equals 1 is not established (body 1162-1165). (e) Fisher p. 355: the 80 per cent band 2.65<=beta_2<=3.42 for the form rests on monotonicity of E_r on each side, not proved (body 1433-1437); the crossing values r=17.172, 14.059, 12.112, 10.985 are asserted without written evaluation or bound. (f) Fisher pp. 354-355 Type II: condition (C) is not verified, so the Type II inverse-information values are not shown to be limit variances of a root of the likelihood equations (body 1437-1442). (g) Grouped normal information at a fixed grid phase: the periodic remainder is bounded only at order a^3 (thm grouped-phase, body 1599-1631; host fisher-grouping 350-359), not small enough to decide the eighth-order terms of thm p15-fg-expansion at a fixed phase; the fixed-grid information to that order is owed. (h) Dilution method p. 366: the efficiency at a given density is the periodic function D^2/(VW); its oscillation is supported at a=2 only by an unwritten 41-phase numerical summation and is unbounded for other a (body 1798-1810); Fisher's 87.71 per cent at a given density is not established with a written bound.
